definition: A colonial species is a species whose members live or breed in groups or colonies in close proximity rather than separately. In this context, colony living can shape social interactions such as competition, dominance, and the chance that young may end up in neighboring nests.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit definition of “colonial species” as living/breeding in groups or colonies in close proximity; it only uses the phrase “cliff-nesting colonial species” in context.

The claim that “colony living can shape social interactions such as competition, dominance” is only indirectly suggested in the study context (siblicidal aggression/adoption) and is not stated as a general property of colonial species in the packet.

The example about “chance that young may end up in neighboring nests” is only supported specifically by this kittiwake adoption scenario (ejected chicks falling into other nests), not as a general feature of colonial species as defined.

The packet supports that the black-legged kittiwake is described as a cliff-nesting colonial species, but it does not establish a general definition of “colonial species” as members that live or breed in close-proximity groups rather than separately.

The added explanation about colony living shaping competition, dominance, and young ending up in neighboring nests goes beyond what is directly supported as a general sense; the packet only discusses sibling aggression, dominance, and adoption in this particular species.
